guide.title: TP-02 E-104: free and check the tight upper punch
guide.summary: The possible cause of alarm E-104 is product fines packed in the upper punch guide or a worn guide bushing. This guide is based on equipment manual section 6.2 and past repeat incidents at station 17.

safety.text: Stop the press with the STOP key and wait up to 30 seconds for the turret to stop completely.
Switch isolator Q1 to OFF, lock it with your padlock, and attach your danger tag.
Press hydraulic release valve V3 until the gauge reads 0 bar.
Press the START key to confirm the machine does not start.
Wear cut-resistant gloves when handling tooling, as punch tips are sharp.
Wear the dust mask and gloves listed in the batch manufacturing record.

steps.text: Open the upper guard.
Turn the turret slowly with handwheel H1, feel for the station that resists, and mark it.
steps.caution: Check station 17 first, as it has repeatedly seized from fine buildup.

steps.text: Remove the upper punch from that station using punch removal tool T-12.
Inspect the punch barrel, head, and tip for scoring, burrs, or a mushroomed head.
steps.caution: Never polish the barrel; replace a damaged punch with upper punch RTP-PN-U-10.

steps.text: Clean the guide bore using a lint-free cloth moistened with 70% IPA.
steps.caution: Never use a metal brush to clean the bore.

steps.text: Check the guide bore with go/no-go gauge G-19.
steps.caution: Cleaning alone does not hold if the bushing is worn. If gauge G-19 fails, escalate to replace bushing RTP-BS-07.

steps.text: Apply 1 drop of food-grade punch oil RTP-LB-02 onto the punch barrel and wipe off the excess.
Refit the upper punch and attach its dust cup RTP-SL-03.
Turn the turret two full turns with handwheel H1 to confirm it turns without resistance.

parts.name: Upper punch, B tooling, 10 mm round

restart_checks.text: Remove all tools and verify every punch and die is in place.
Close all guards and remove personal locks and tags.
Run the turret empty at 10 rpm for 2 minutes and listen for abnormal noise.
Run the first tablets and deliver them to QA for weight, thickness, and hardness checks.
Perform line clearance as per the plant SOP.
Record the repair details, parts used, and downtime in the equipment logbook.

escalate_if: Go/no-go gauge G-19 does not pass the guide bore check (maintenance engineer required for bushing replacement).
The upper punch barrel, head, or tip is damaged and no replacement punch is available.
The turret continues to resist rotation after cleaning, lubrication, and reassembly.
W-212 compression force deviation warnings appeared more than 10 times in an hour prior to the stop.
QA rejects the initial tablets during in-process checks.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.2 E-104 Upper punch tight
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-104 PUNCH TIGHT, the turret stops and the main drive torque is high. Likely causes: product fines packed in an upper punch guide bore; too little punch lubrication; a scored, burred or mushroomed punch; a worn guide bushing; wear on the upper cam track. Procedure: 1. Lock out the press (section 1.2). 2. Open the upper guard. Turn the turret slowly with handwheel H1 and feel for the station that resists; mark it. 3. Remove the upper punch from that station with punch removal tool T-12. 4. Inspect the punch barrel, head and tip for scoring, burrs or a mushroomed head. A damaged punch must be replaced with upper punch RTP-PN-U-10; never polish the barrel. 5. Clean the guide bore with a lint-free cloth moistened with 70% IPA. Never use a metal brush. 6. Check the bore with go/no-go gauge G-19. If the gauge does not pass, the guide bushing is worn: replace bushing RTP-BS-07 (maintenance engineer only, section 9.4). 7. Put 1 drop of food-grade punch oil RTP-LB-02 on the punch barrel and wipe off the excess. 8. Refit the punch and its dust cup RTP-SL-03. Turn the turret two full turns with H1: it must turn without resistance. Typical time: 45 minutes for one station; about 3 hours if a guide bushing must be replaced.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.3 E-118 Lower punch tight or ejection fault
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-118, the turret stops at ejection or a lower punch sticks below the die table. Likely causes: powder under the die table, a lower punch with a damaged tip or barrel, a worn ejection cam, a die not seated flush. Procedure: 1. Lock out the press (section 1.2). 2. Remove the die table scraper and vacuum the powder from the lower turret. 3. Turn the turret with handwheel H1 and find the tight lower punch. 4. Remove it through the lower punch access door with tool T-14 and inspect it. Replace a damaged punch with lower punch RTP-PN-L-10. 5. Check that the die is flush with the die table using the dial gauge: maximum 0.05 mm proud. Reseat or replace die RTP-DI-10. 6. Inspect the ejection cam for grooves; report wear to the engineer. Typical time: 50 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.1 Alarm list
manual_sections.text: Alarms starting with E stop the press. Alarms starting with W are warnings: the press keeps running but the cause must be checked. E-104 Upper punch tight. E-118 Lower punch tight or ejection fault. E-150 Guard open. E-221 Main drive overload. E-330 Feed frame motor fault. W-212 Compression force deviation. W-305 Lubrication pressure low. W-401 Hopper level low.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.5 W-212 Compression force deviation
manual_sections.text: Warning W-212 appears when the main compression force is more than 10% away from the set point over 50 tablets. The press keeps running. Likely causes: uneven die fill (hopper level, feed frame paddle speed, poor powder flow), lower punches of unequal working length, fines building up in punch guides. First actions: check the hopper level and feed frame speed; weigh 20 tablets and compare with the batch record limits. If W-212 appears more than 10 times in an hour, check punch working length with gauge G-21 at the next stop. Rising W-212 counts together with a higher main drive torque often come before an E-104 punch tight stop.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.4 E-221 Main drive overload
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-221, the motor protection relay F3 trips and the press stops. Likely causes: over-compression after a tablet thickness change, tight punches (see E-104 and E-118), a jammed feed frame, a slipping or worn V-belt. Procedure: 1. Check the compression force history on the HMI: forces above the maximum for the tooling point to over-compression; correct the thickness setting to the value in the batch record. 2. Lock out the press (section 1.2) and turn the turret one full turn with handwheel H1; any tight station must be cleared first. 3. Check V-belt tension: deflection 8 to 10 mm when pressed with 50 N at the middle of the span. Replace a cracked or glazed belt with RTP-BT-04. 4. Let the motor cool for at least 10 minutes, then reset relay F3. 5. Restart at 20 rpm and increase speed in steps while watching the compression force. Typical time: 30 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.7 E-330 Feed frame motor fault
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-330, the feed frame paddles stop and the press stops. Likely causes: powder packed in the feed frame, a loose drive coupling, a failed motor drive. Procedure: 1. Lock out the press (section 1.2). 2. Remove the feed frame and clean the paddles and housing. 3. Check the drive coupling for play and tighten its clamping screws to 6 Nm. 4. Check the paddle set for bent or worn blades; replace with paddle set RTP-FF-11. 5. Refit the feed frame with 0.1 mm clearance to the die table (feeler gauge). Typical time: 40 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 1.2 Lockout before opening any guard
manual_sections.text: Never open a guard or put hands near the turret while the press can move. 1. Stop the press with the STOP key and wait until the turret has stopped completely (rundown takes up to 30 seconds). 2. Switch the main isolator Q1 to OFF and lock it with your personal padlock. Attach a danger tag with your name. 3. Press the hydraulic pressure release valve V3 until the gauge reads 0 bar. 4. Check for zero energy: press START; the press must not start. 5. Punch tips and die edges are sharp: wear cut-resistant gloves when handling tooling. 6. Wear the dust mask and gloves listed in the batch manufacturing record for the product on the press.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 9.6 Return to service after a repair
manual_sections.text: 1. Remove all tools and check that every punch and die is in place. 2. Close all guards and remove your lock and tag. 3. Run the turret empty at 10 rpm for 2 minutes and listen for abnormal noise. 4. Run the first tablets and give them to QA for in-process checks (weight, thickness, hardness) before the batch continues. 5. Do line clearance as per the plant SOP. 6. Record the repair, the parts used and the downtime in the equipment logbook.

guide.title: AC-2 Door seal fault: inspect and replace door gasket
guide.summary: A possible cause is a cut, flattened, or hardened door gasket, particularly near the door hinge. This guide is based on equipment manual section 4.2 for E-07 door seal faults and past incident PHA-0028.

safety.text: Never open the door unless the chamber pressure gauge reads 0 bar and chamber temperature is below 80 °C.
Close and lock steam supply valve SV-1, switch electrical isolator Q0 to OFF and lock it, and attach danger tags.
Open the chamber vent valve and confirm chamber and jacket pressure gauges both read 0 bar before opening the door.
Wear heat-resistant gloves and a face shield because pipes, door, and chamber surfaces stay hot.

steps.text: End or abort the cycle and lock out steam valve SV-1 and electrical isolator Q0.
steps.caution: Verify both chamber and jacket pressure gauges read 0 bar and temperature is below 80 °C.

steps.text: Open the sterilizer door carefully.
Inspect the whole gasket for cuts, flat spots, and hardening, checking especially near the hinge area.
Remove the old gasket from the door frame groove.
Clean the gasket groove thoroughly with a lint-free cloth and water for injection.
Press the new door gasket SA-DG-600 evenly into the groove starting at the top centre.
Apply a thin film of approved silicone grease SA-SG-01 onto the installed gasket.
Check that the compressed air supply reads at least 5 bar.

parts.why: Replace cut or damaged door gasket
parts.name: Door gasket, inflatable silicone
Silicone grease, approved for sterilizer seals

restart_checks.text: Remove locks and tags, open steam valve SV-1 slowly, and allow the jacket to heat up.
Run a vacuum leak test and confirm the leak rate is 1.3 mbar/min or less.
Run a Bowie-Dick test cycle and verify the indicator sheet shows an even colour change.
Obtain QA review and release before returning the sterilizer to production.
Record the repair, test results, and downtime in the equipment logbook.

escalate_if: The vacuum leak test rate exceeds 1.3 mbar/min after gasket replacement.
The Bowie-Dick test fails or shows an uneven colour change.

manual_sections.manual_title: Sterimax SA-600 Steam Sterilizer: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 4.2 E-07 Door seal fault
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-07, door seal pressure not reached within 60 seconds of cycle start; the cycle does not start or is aborted. Likely causes: a cut, flattened or hardened door gasket; dirt in the gasket groove; low compressed air supply (below 5 bar); a faulty seal supply valve. Procedure: 1. Lock out the sterilizer and make sure the chamber is at 0 bar and below 80 °C (section 1.4). 2. Inspect the whole gasket for cuts, flat spots and hardening, especially near the hinge. 3. Clean the groove with a lint-free cloth and water for injection. 4. Replace a damaged gasket with door gasket SA-DG-600: press it evenly into the groove starting at the top centre, and apply a thin film of approved silicone grease SA-SG-01. 5. Check compressed air supply is at least 5 bar. 6. Run a vacuum leak test (limit 1.3 mbar/min) and a Bowie-Dick test; both must pass before the sterilizer is released. Typical time: 90 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Sterimax SA-600 Steam Sterilizer: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 1.4 Pressure, steam and lockout
manual_sections.text: The chamber and jacket hold steam under pressure. 1. Never try to open the door unless the chamber pressure gauge reads 0 bar and the chamber temperature is below 80 °C. 2. Before any repair, end or abort the cycle, close the steam supply valve SV-1 and lock it; switch the electrical isolator Q0 to OFF and lock it; attach danger tags. 3. Open the chamber vent valve and wait until the chamber and jacket gauges both read 0 bar. 4. Pipes, door and chamber surfaces stay hot: wear heat-resistant gloves and a face shield.

manual_sections.manual_title: Sterimax SA-600 Steam Sterilizer: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 4.3 E-12 Vacuum level not reached
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-12, the chamber does not reach the pre-vacuum set point; the cycle aborts. Likely causes: no seal water to the liquid ring vacuum pump, an air leak at the door gasket or a valve, a worn vacuum pump. Procedure: 1. Check the seal water flow to the vacuum pump (sight glass must show flow). 2. Run a vacuum leak test: above 1.3 mbar/min means a leak; check the door gasket first (section 4.2). 3. If there is no leak, ask maintenance to service the pump with kit SA-VP-KIT. Typical time: 60 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Sterimax SA-600 Steam Sterilizer: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 2.1 Machine overview
manual_sections.text: The SA-600 is a jacketed steam sterilizer with a hinged door. The door seals with an inflatable silicone gasket that sits in a groove around the door frame and is pressed against the door by compressed air during the cycle. A liquid ring vacuum pump removes air during the pre-vacuum pulses. Condensate leaves the chamber through the drain, where a PT100 sensor measures drain temperature, then through strainer ST-2 and the steam trap.

manual_sections.manual_title: Sterimax SA-600 Steam Sterilizer: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.1 Return to service after a repair
manual_sections.text: 1. Remove locks and tags, open SV-1 slowly and let the jacket heat up. 2. Run a vacuum leak test: the leak rate must be 1.3 mbar/min or less. 3. Run a Bowie-Dick test cycle: the indicator sheet must show an even colour change. 4. QA reviews the test results and releases the sterilizer. 5. Record the repair, tests and downtime in the equipment logbook.

manual_sections.manual_title: Sterimax SA-600 Steam Sterilizer: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 4.5 W-05 Jacket pressure slow rise
manual_sections.text: Warning W-05 appears when the jacket takes more than 10 minutes to reach working pressure. The cycle continues but takes longer. First actions: check the plant steam supply pressure; check the jacket steam trap and strainer for blockage. Repeated W-05 warnings often come before E-21 drain temperature faults.

guide.title: BL-3 Forming Temperature Alarm and Shallow Pockets: Test and Replace Forming Heater Cartridge
guide.summary: Shallow blister pockets followed by a forming temperature alarm indicate a possible cause of a failed forming heater cartridge or loose thermocouple. This guide follows manual section 5.2 and repeat incident PHA-0026 where cartridge no. 3 failed. Typical repair time is 60 minutes.

safety.text: Stop the machine with the STOP key at the end of a cycle.
Turn main switch S0 to OFF, lock it with your personal padlock, and attach a danger tag.
Close the compressed air ball valve and open dump valve DV1 until the air gauge reads 0 bar.
Wait until plate temperature display drops below 50 °C or wear heat-resistant gloves.
Press START to check for zero energy; ensure the machine does not move.

steps.text: Lock out the machine and let the forming plates cool down.
steps.caution: Plates run at up to 160 °C; wait until below 50 °C or wear heat-resistant gloves.

steps.text: Disconnect the heater cartridges at the terminal box.
Measure each heater cartridge with a meter to verify it reads 40 to 50 ohm.
steps.caution: An open circuit reading means the cartridge has failed.

steps.text: Replace any failed cartridge with a new heater cartridge BPM-HC-250.
Check that the thermocouple sits fully in its bore and its clamp is tight.
Refit the thermocouple with heat-transfer paste BPM-HP-02, or replace with BPM-TC-K2 if damaged.
Ask an electrician to check solid-state relay BPM-SSR-40 if cartridges and thermocouple are good.
Heat up the machine for 20 minutes.
Check blister pocket depth on 10 strips.

restart_checks.text: Remove tools, close guards, and remove personal lock and tag.
Heat up the machine for 20 minutes.
Run empty strips and check pocket shape, seal pattern, and batch code.
Perform a blue dye leak test on 20 blisters from each lane; all must pass before feeding tablets.
Obtain QA check on the first cards before continuing the batch.
Complete line clearance per plant SOP and record the repair in the equipment logbook.

escalate_if: Heater cartridges and thermocouple test good but forming plate still fails to heat up.
Forming plate temperature remains more than 10 °C below set point after replacement.
Pocket depth on 10 strips remains shallow or uneven after the 20-minute heat-up.
Blue dye leak test fails on any of the 20 blisters from each lane.

manual_sections.manual_title: Vireo BPM-250 Blister Packing Machine: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 5.2 E-31 Forming heater temperature low
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-31, forming plate temperature more than 10 °C below the set point; pockets come out shallow or uneven and the machine stops. Likely causes: a failed heater cartridge, a loose or failed thermocouple, a failed solid-state relay. Procedure: 1. Lock out the machine and let the plates cool (section 1.3). 2. Disconnect the heater cartridges at the terminal box and measure each one: a good cartridge reads 40 to 50 ohm; open circuit means failed. Replace a failed cartridge with BPM-HC-250 (250 W, 230 V). 3. Check that the thermocouple sits fully in its bore and the clamp is tight. Refit it with heat-transfer paste BPM-HP-02; replace a damaged thermocouple with BPM-TC-K2. 4. If cartridges and thermocouple are good, ask the electrician to check solid-state relay BPM-SSR-40. 5. Heat up for 20 minutes and check pocket depth on 10 strips. Typical time: 60 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Vireo BPM-250 Blister Packing Machine: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 5.3 E-44 Sealing temperature deviation
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-44, sealing plate temperature outside set point plus or minus 5 °C; risk of leaking blisters. The machine stops. Likely causes: failed sealing heater cartridge, thermocouple not in contact, display showing the controller set point instead of the actual temperature. Procedure: 1. Lock out and cool down (section 1.3). 2. Measure the sealing heater cartridges (40 to 50 ohm). Replace failed ones with BPM-HC-250. 3. Reseat the thermocouple with heat-transfer paste BPM-HP-02. 4. After heat-up, check the plate surface temperature with a calibrated contact thermometer; it must be within 5 °C of the set point. 5. Run a blue dye leak test on 20 blisters from each lane before restarting the batch. Typical time: 60 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Vireo BPM-250 Blister Packing Machine: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 5.4 E-52 Film web break
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-52, the PVC web is broken or the film reel has run out; the machine stops. Likely causes: a bad splice, too high web tension, a worn or seized guide roller, film stuck to a hot forming plate. Procedure: 1. Lock out the machine (section 1.3). 2. Remove the broken film from the forming station. 3. Rethread the film along the path shown in the figure, under the dancer arm. 4. Check every guide roller turns freely; replace a seized roller with BPM-GR-08. 5. Join the film with splice tape, keeping the splice straight. 6. Run 5 empty cycles at low speed and check the web runs centred. Typical time: 20 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Vireo BPM-250 Blister Packing Machine: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 5.5 W-12 Film tracking deviation

guide.title: TP-01 W-305: Refill oil and restore central lubrication pressure
guide.summary: A possible cause is low oil level in the central lubrication reservoir or air in the lines. This guide is based on manual procedure 6.6 and plant incident PHA-0030.

safety.text: Stop the press with the STOP key and wait up to 30 seconds until the turret stops completely.
Turn main isolator Q1 to OFF, lock it with your padlock, and attach your danger tag.
Press hydraulic pressure release valve V3 until the gauge reads 0 bar.
Press START to verify zero energy; the press must not start.
Wear cut-resistant gloves when handling tooling, and wear the dust mask and gloves specified in the batch record.

steps.text: Lock out the tablet press following all lockout points.
Check the oil level in the central lubrication reservoir.
Top up the central lubrication reservoir using only oil RTP-LB-01.
steps.caution: Use only oil RTP-LB-01; running with low pressure leads to punch tightness E-104.

steps.text: Inspect all lubrication lines and the distributor block for leaks or blockages.
Remove lockout padlocks, close guards, and power on the machine.
Run the lubrication pump manually from the maintenance screen until pressure is above 2 bar.

restart_checks.text: Remove all tools and check that every punch and die is in place.
Close all guards and remove your lock and tag.
Run the turret empty at 10 rpm for 2 minutes and listen for abnormal noise.
Run the first tablets and give them to QA for in-process checks before the batch continues.
Perform line clearance as per the plant SOP.
Record the repair, the parts used, and the downtime in the equipment logbook.

escalate_if: Lubrication pressure cannot reach above 2 bar after refilling and running the pump.
Oil leaks or damaged lines are observed at the distributor block.
Punches feel tight when turning the turret or alarm E-104 appears.
Abnormal noises are heard during the 2-minute empty run.

manual_sections.title: 6.6 W-305 Lubrication pressure low
manual_sections.text: Warning W-305 appears when the central lubrication pressure is below 2 bar. The press keeps running, but punch guides and cam tracks are no longer oiled. Running for long with W-305 leads to punch tightness (E-104). First actions: check the oil level in the central lubrication reservoir and top up with oil RTP-LB-01 only. manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.2 E-104 Upper punch tight
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-104 PUNCH TIGHT, the turret stops and the main drive torque is high. Likely causes: product fines packed in an upper punch guide bore; too little punch lubrication; a scored, burred or mushroomed punch; a worn guide bushing; wear on the upper cam track. Procedure: 1. Lock out the press (section 1.2). 2. Open the upper guard. Turn the turret slowly with handwheel H1 and feel for the station that resists; mark it. 3. Remove the upper punch from that station with punch removal tool T-12. 4. Inspect the punch barrel, head and tip for scoring, burrs or a mushroomed head. A damaged punch must be replaced with upper punch RTP-PN-U-10; never polish the barrel. 5. Clean the guide bore with a lint-free cloth moistened with 70% IPA. Never use a metal brush. 6. Check the bore with go/no-go gauge G-19. If the gauge does not pass, the guide bushing is worn: replace bushing RTP-BS-07 (maintenance engineer only, section 9.4). 7. Put 1 drop of food-grade punch oil RTP-LB-02 on the punch barrel and wipe off the excess. 8. Refit the punch and its dust cup RTP-SL-03. Turn the turret two full turns with H1: it must turn without resistance. Typical time: 45 minutes for one station; about 3 hours if a guide bushing must be replaced.

manual_sections.title: 1.2 Lockout before opening any guard
manual_sections.text: Never open a guard or put hands near the turret while the press can move. 1. Stop the press with the STOP key and wait until the turret has stopped completely (rundown takes up to 30 seconds). 2. Switch the main isolator Q1 to OFF and lock it with your personal padlock. Attach a danger tag with your name. 3. Press the hydraulic pressure release valve V3 until the gauge reads 0 bar. 4. Check for zero energy: press START; the press must not start. 5. Punch tips and die edges are sharp: wear cut-resistant gloves when handling tooling. 6. Wear the dust mask and gloves listed in the batch manufacturing record for the product on the press.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.3 E-118 Lower punch tight or ejection fault
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-118, the turret stops at ejection or a lower punch sticks below the die table. Likely causes: powder under the die table, a lower punch with a damaged tip or barrel, a worn ejection cam, a die not seated flush. Procedure: 1. Lock out the press (section 1.2). 2. Remove the die table scraper and vacuum the powder from the lower turret. 3. Turn the turret with handwheel H1 and find the tight lower punch. 4. Remove it through the lower punch access door with tool T-14 and inspect it. Replace a damaged punch with lower punch RTP-PN-L-10. 5. Check that the die is flush with the die table using the dial gauge: maximum 0.05 mm proud. Reseat or replace die RTP-DI-10. 6. Inspect the ejection cam for grooves; report wear to the engineer. Typical time: 50 minutes.

manual_sections.title: 6.7 E-330 Feed frame motor fault
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-330, the feed frame paddles stop and the press stops. Likely causes: powder packed in the feed frame, a loose drive coupling, a failed motor drive. Check the paddle set for bent or worn blades; replace with paddle set RTP-FF-11. 5. Refit the feed frame with 0.1 mm clearance to the die table (feeler gauge). Typical time: 40 minutes.

guide.title: AC-2 E-12: check seal water, vacuum leak rate, and door gasket
guide.summary: Alarm E-12 indicates the chamber did not reach the pre-vacuum set point, leading to an aborted cycle. A possible cause is a lack of seal water to the vacuum pump, an air leak at the door gasket or a valve, or a worn pump. This guide follows the standard troubleshooting steps from the equipment manual.

safety.text: Never try to open the door unless chamber pressure is 0 bar and chamber temperature is below 80 °C.
Before repairs, end or abort the cycle, close steam supply valve SV-1, switch electrical isolator Q0 to OFF, and lock both.
Attach danger tags to locked isolators.
Open the chamber vent valve and confirm chamber and jacket gauges read 0 bar.
Wear heat-resistant gloves and a face shield because pipes, door, and chamber surfaces stay hot.

steps.text: Check the seal water flow to the vacuum pump through the sight glass.
steps.caution: The sight glass must show flow.

steps.text: Run a vacuum leak test on the sterilizer.
steps.caution: A leak rate above 1.3 mbar/min means there is an air leak.

steps.text: If the leak rate is above 1.3 mbar/min, inspect the inflatable door gasket for damage or leaks.
If the door gasket is damaged, replace it with new door gasket SA-DG-600.
If there is no leak found, service the vacuum pump using kit SA-VP-KIT.

restart_checks.text: Remove locks and tags, open valve SV-1 slowly, and allow the jacket to heat up.
Run a vacuum leak test and confirm the leak rate is 1.3 mbar/min or less.
Run a Bowie-Dick test cycle and verify the indicator sheet shows an even colour change.
Obtain QA review and release before returning the sterilizer to production.
Record the repair, test results, and downtime in the equipment logbook.

escalate_if: No seal water flow is visible in the sight glass and supply cannot be restored.
The vacuum leak test rate remains above 1.3 mbar/min after replacing the door gasket.
Bowie-Dick test cycle fails or shows uneven colour change.
Pump replacement or service kit SA-VP-KIT does not resolve alarm E-12.
open_questions: What was the active cycle phase and chamber pressure reading when alarm E-12 was triggered?
Was any product load inside the autoclave during the aborted cycle, and has it been quarantined by QA?

manual_sections.title: 4.3 E-12 Vacuum level not reached
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-12, the chamber does not reach the pre-vacuum set point; the cycle aborts. Likely causes: no seal water to the liquid ring vacuum pump, an air leak at the door gasket or a valve, a worn vacuum pump. Procedure: 1. manual_sections.manual_title: Sterimax SA-600 Steam Sterilizer: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 2.1 Machine overview
manual_sections.text: The SA-600 is a jacketed steam sterilizer with a hinged door. The door seals with an inflatable silicone gasket that sits in a groove around the door frame and is pressed against the door by compressed air during the cycle. A liquid ring vacuum pump removes air during the pre-vacuum pulses. Condensate leaves the chamber through the drain, where a PT100 sensor measures drain temperature, then through strainer ST-2 and the steam trap.

manual_sections.manual_title: Sterimax SA-600 Steam Sterilizer: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 4.4 E-21 Drain temperature low
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-21, drain temperature below 121 °C during the exposure phase; the cycle aborts and the load is not sterile. Likely causes: strainer ST-2 blocked with scale, a stuck steam trap, wet steam. Procedure: 1. Lock out the sterilizer (section 1.4). 2. Open the strainer cap and clean screen ST-2; replace a damaged screen with SA-STR-2. 3. Blow down the steam trap; replace a trap that stays closed with SA-ST-15. 4. Check the PT100 drain sensor reading against a calibrated probe; replace a faulty sensor with SA-PT100. 5. Run one empty cycle and check drain temperature stays at or above 121 °C for the whole exposure. The aborted load must be treated as not sterile and reported to QA. Typical time: 60 minutes.

manual_sections.title: 4.5 W-05 Jacket pressure slow rise
manual_sections.text: Warning W-05 appears when the jacket takes more than 10 minutes to reach working pressure. The cycle continues but takes longer. First actions: check the plant steam supply pressure; check the jacket steam trap and strainer for blockage. Repeated W-05 warnings often come before E-21 drain temperature faults.

Run a Bowie-Dick test cycle: the indicator sheet must show an even colour change. 4. QA reviews the test results and releases the sterilizer. 5. Record the repair, tests and downtime in the equipment logbook.

manual_sections.title: 4.6 W-09 Feed water conductivity high
manual_sections.text: Warning W-09 appears when the steam generator feed water conductivity is above 5 µS/cm. Scale and poor steam quality follow. First actions: inform the water system owner; check the purified water supply; increase blowdown frequency as per the maintenance plan.

manual_sections.title: 1.4 Pressure, steam and lockout
manual_sections.text: The chamber and jacket hold steam under pressure. 1. Never try to open the door unless the chamber pressure gauge reads 0 bar and the chamber temperature is below 80 °C. 2. Before any repair, end or abort the cycle, close the steam supply valve SV-1 and lock it; switch the electrical isolator Q0 to OFF and lock it; attach danger tags. 3. Open the chamber vent valve and wait until the chamber and jacket gauges both read 0 bar. 4. Pipes, door and chamber surfaces stay hot: wear heat-resistant gloves and a face shield.

safety.text: Stop the press with the STOP key and wait up to 30 seconds until the turret stops completely.

Turn the turret slowly with handwheel H1 and feel for the station that resists, then mark it.
Remove the upper punch from that station using punch removal tool T-12.
Inspect the punch barrel, head, and tip for scoring, burrs, or a mushroomed head.

steps.text: If damaged, replace the upper punch with upper punch RTP-PN-U-10.

steps.text: Check the guide bore with go/no-go gauge G-19.

manual_sections.manual_title: Sterimax SA-600 Steam Sterilizer: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 4.2 E-07 Door seal fault
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-07, door seal pressure not reached within 60 seconds of cycle start; the cycle does not start or is aborted. Likely causes: a cut, flattened or hardened door gasket; dirt in the gasket groove; low compressed air supply (below 5 bar); a faulty seal supply valve. Procedure: 1. Lock out the sterilizer and make sure the chamber is at 0 bar and below 80 °C (section 1.4). 2. Inspect the whole gasket for cuts, flat spots and hardening, especially near the hinge. 3. Clean the groove with a lint-free cloth and water for injection. 4. Replace a damaged gasket with door gasket SA-DG-600: press it evenly into the groove starting at the top centre, and apply a thin film of approved silicone grease SA-SG-01. 5. Check compressed air supply is at least 5 bar. 6. Run a vacuum leak test (limit 1.3 mbar/min) and a Bowie-Dick test; both must pass before the sterilizer is released. Typical time: 90 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Sterimax SA-600 Steam Sterilizer: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 1.4 Pressure, steam and lockout
manual_sections.text: The chamber and jacket hold steam under pressure. 1. Never try to open the door unless the chamber pressure gauge reads 0 bar and the chamber temperature is below 80 °C. 2. Before any repair, end or abort the cycle, close the steam supply valve SV-1 and lock it; switch the electrical isolator Q0 to OFF and lock it; attach danger tags. 3. Open the chamber vent valve and wait until the chamber and jacket gauges both read 0 bar. 4. Pipes, door and chamber surfaces stay hot: wear heat-resistant gloves and a face shield.

manual_sections.title: 4.3 E-12 Vacuum level not reached
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-12, the chamber does not reach the pre-vacuum set point; the cycle aborts. Likely causes: no seal water to the liquid ring vacuum pump, an air leak at the door gasket or a valve, a worn vacuum pump. Procedure: 1. Check the seal water flow to the vacuum pump (sight glass must show flow). 2. Run a vacuum leak test: above 1.3 mbar/min means a leak; check the door gasket first (section 4.2). 3. If there is no leak, ask maintenance to service the pump with kit SA-VP-KIT. Typical time: 60 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Sterimax SA-600 Steam Sterilizer: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 2.1 Machine overview
manual_sections.text: The SA-600 is a jacketed steam sterilizer with a hinged door. The door seals with an inflatable silicone gasket that sits in a groove around the door frame and is pressed against the door by compressed air during the cycle. A liquid ring vacuum pump removes air during the pre-vacuum pulses. Condensate leaves the chamber through the drain, where a PT100 sensor measures drain temperature, then through strainer ST-2 and the steam trap.

guide.title: BL-3 Forming Temperature Alarm: Inspect and Replace Forming Heater Cartridge or Thermocouple
guide.summary: A possible cause is an open-circuit forming heater cartridge or a loose thermocouple causing shallow blister pockets and a temperature drop. This repair guide is based on manual procedure 5.2 for alarm E-31 and previous plant incident record PHA-0026. Technicians will test the heater elements, verify the sensor, and perform return-to-service checks.

safety.text: Stop the machine with the STOP key at the end of a cycle.
Switch the main switch S0 to OFF, attach your personal padlock, and fit a danger tag.
Close the compressed air ball valve and open dump valve DV1 until the pressure gauge reads 0 bar.
Press START to verify zero energy; the machine must not move.
Wait until the plate temperature drops below 50 °C on the display or wear heat-resistant gloves.

steps.text: Perform lockout and tagout on the machine and dump the compressed air to 0 bar.
steps.caution: Plates can reach 160 °C; let them cool below 50 °C before touching.

steps.text: Disconnect the forming plate heater cartridges inside the terminal box.
Measure the resistance of each heater cartridge using a multimeter.
steps.caution: A good cartridge reads 40 to 50 ohm; an open-circuit reading indicates a failed heater.

steps.text: Replace any failed heater cartridge with a new heater cartridge BPM-HC-250.
Check that the thermocouple sits fully inside its bore and ensure its clamp is tight.
Apply heat-transfer paste BPM-HP-02 and refit the thermocouple into the plate bore.
Replace the thermocouple with part BPM-TC-K2 if the sensor or cable is damaged.
Reconnect all wiring securely inside the terminal box.

restart_checks.text: Remove all tools, close safety guards, and remove personal lock and tag.
Power on the machine and allow the heating plates to heat up for 20 minutes.
Check pocket depth on 10 strips after heating.
Run empty strips and inspect pocket shape, seal pattern, and batch code embossing.
Perform a blue dye leak test on 20 blisters from each lane; all must pass before feeding tablets.
Obtain QA approval on the first blister cards before continuing production.
Complete line clearance as per the plant SOP and log the maintenance action in the equipment logbook.

escalate_if: All heater cartridges measure between 40 and 50 ohm and the thermocouple is intact (electrician must inspect solid-state relay BPM-SSR-40).
The forming plate temperature does not reach the set point within 20 minutes of warm-up.
Forming pockets remain shallow or uneven on the 10 test strips after replacing components.
Any blister fails the 20-blister per lane blue dye leak test.

manual_sections.title: 5.2 E-31 Forming heater temperature low
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-31, forming plate temperature more than 10 °C below the set point; pockets come out shallow or uneven and the machine stops. Likely causes: a failed heater cartridge, a loose or failed thermocouple, a failed solid-state relay. Procedure: 1. Lock out the machine and let the plates cool (section 1.3). 2. Disconnect the heater cartridges at the terminal box and measure each one: a good cartridge reads 40 to 50 ohm; open circuit means failed. Refit it with heat-transfer paste BPM-HP-02; replace a damaged thermocouple with BPM-TC-K2. 4. If cartridges and thermocouple are good, ask the electrician to check solid-state relay BPM-SSR-40. 5. Heat up for 20 minutes and check pocket depth on 10 strips. Typical time: 60 minutes.

manual_sections.title: 5.3 E-44 Sealing temperature deviation
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-44, sealing plate temperature outside set point plus or minus 5 °C; risk of leaking blisters. The machine stops. Likely causes: failed sealing heater cartridge, thermocouple not in contact, display showing the controller set point instead of the actual temperature. Procedure: 1. After heat-up, check the plate surface temperature with a calibrated contact thermometer; it must be within 5 °C of the set point. 5. Run a blue dye leak test on 20 blisters from each lane before restarting the batch. Typical time: 60 minutes.

manual_sections.title: 5.4 E-52 Film web break
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-52, the PVC web is broken or the film reel has run out; the machine stops. Likely causes: a bad splice, too high web tension, a worn or seized guide roller, film stuck to a hot forming plate. Procedure: 1. Lock out the machine (section 1.3). 2. Remove the broken film from the forming station. 3. Rethread the film along the path shown in the figure, under the dancer arm. 4. Check every guide roller turns freely; replace a seized roller with BPM-GR-08. 5. Join the film with splice tape, keeping the splice straight. 6. Run 5 empty cycles at low speed and check the web runs centred. Typical time: 20 minutes.

manual_sections.title: 5.5 W-12 Film tracking deviation

manual_sections.manual_title: Sterimax SA-600 Steam Sterilizer: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 2.1 Machine overview
manual_sections.text: The SA-600 is a jacketed steam sterilizer with a hinged door. The door seals with an inflatable silicone gasket that sits in a groove around the door frame and is pressed against the door by compressed air during the cycle. A liquid ring vacuum pump removes air during the pre-vacuum pulses. Condensate leaves the chamber through the drain, where a PT100 sensor measures drain temperature, then through strainer ST-2 and the steam trap.

manual_sections.title: 4.4 E-21 Drain temperature low
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-21, drain temperature below 121 °C during the exposure phase; the cycle aborts and the load is not sterile. Check the PT100 drain sensor reading against a calibrated probe; replace a faulty sensor with SA-PT100. 5. Run one empty cycle and check drain temperature stays at or above 121 °C for the whole exposure. The aborted load must be treated as not sterile and reported to QA. Typical time: 60 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.2 E-104 Upper punch tight
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-104 PUNCH TIGHT, the turret stops and the main drive torque is high. Likely causes: product fines packed in an upper punch guide bore; too little punch lubrication; a scored, burred or mushroomed punch; a worn guide bushing; wear on the upper cam track. Procedure: 1. Lock out the press (section 1.2). 2. Open the upper guard. Turn the turret slowly with handwheel H1 and feel for the station that resists; mark it. 3. Remove the upper punch from that station with punch removal tool T-12. 4. Inspect the punch barrel, head and tip for scoring, burrs or a mushroomed head. A damaged punch must be replaced with upper punch RTP-PN-U-10; never polish the barrel. 5. Clean the guide bore with a lint-free cloth moistened with 70% IPA. Never use a metal brush. 6. Check the bore with go/no-go gauge G-19. If the gauge does not pass, the guide bushing is worn: replace bushing RTP-BS-07 (maintenance engineer only, section 9.4). 7. Put 1 drop of food-grade punch oil RTP-LB-02 on the punch barrel and wipe off the excess. 8. Refit the punch and its dust cup RTP-SL-03. Turn the turret two full turns with H1: it must turn without resistance. Typical time: 45 minutes for one station; about 3 hours if a guide bushing must be replaced.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.3 E-118 Lower punch tight or ejection fault
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-118, the turret stops at ejection or a lower punch sticks below the die table. Likely causes: powder under the die table, a lower punch with a damaged tip or barrel, a worn ejection cam, a die not seated flush. Procedure: 1. Lock out the press (section 1.2). 2. Remove the die table scraper and vacuum the powder from the lower turret. 3. Turn the turret with handwheel H1 and find the tight lower punch. 4. Remove it through the lower punch access door with tool T-14 and inspect it. Replace a damaged punch with lower punch RTP-PN-L-10. 5. Check that the die is flush with the die table using the dial gauge: maximum 0.05 mm proud. Reseat or replace die RTP-DI-10. 6. Inspect the ejection cam for grooves; report wear to the engineer. Typical time: 50 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.1 Alarm list
manual_sections.text: Alarms starting with E stop the press. Alarms starting with W are warnings: the press keeps running but the cause must be checked. E-104 Upper punch tight. E-118 Lower punch tight or ejection fault. E-150 Guard open. E-221 Main drive overload. E-330 Feed frame motor fault. W-212 Compression force deviation. W-305 Lubrication pressure low. W-401 Hopper level low.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.5 W-212 Compression force deviation
manual_sections.text: Warning W-212 appears when the main compression force is more than 10% away from the set point over 50 tablets. The press keeps running. Likely causes: uneven die fill (hopper level, feed frame paddle speed, poor powder flow), lower punches of unequal working length, fines building up in punch guides. First actions: check the hopper level and feed frame speed; weigh 20 tablets and compare with the batch record limits. If W-212 appears more than 10 times in an hour, check punch working length with gauge G-21 at the next stop. Rising W-212 counts together with a higher main drive torque often come before an E-104 punch tight stop.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.4 E-221 Main drive overload
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-221, the motor protection relay F3 trips and the press stops. Likely causes: over-compression after a tablet thickness change, tight punches (see E-104 and E-118), a jammed feed frame, a slipping or worn V-belt. Procedure: 1. Check the compression force history on the HMI: forces above the maximum for the tooling point to over-compression; correct the thickness setting to the value in the batch record. 2. Lock out the press (section 1.2) and turn the turret one full turn with handwheel H1; any tight station must be cleared first. 3. Check V-belt tension: deflection 8 to 10 mm when pressed with 50 N at the middle of the span. Replace a cracked or glazed belt with RTP-BT-04. 4. Let the motor cool for at least 10 minutes, then reset relay F3. 5. Restart at 20 rpm and increase speed in steps while watching the compression force. Typical time: 30 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.7 E-330 Feed frame motor fault
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-330, the feed frame paddles stop and the press stops. Likely causes: powder packed in the feed frame, a loose drive coupling, a failed motor drive. Procedure: 1. Lock out the press (section 1.2). 2. Remove the feed frame and clean the paddles and housing. 3. Check the drive coupling for play and tighten its clamping screws to 6 Nm. 4. Check the paddle set for bent or worn blades; replace with paddle set RTP-FF-11. 5. Refit the feed frame with 0.1 mm clearance to the die table (feeler gauge). Typical time: 40 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 1.2 Lockout before opening any guard
manual_sections.text: Never open a guard or put hands near the turret while the press can move. 1. Stop the press with the STOP key and wait until the turret has stopped completely (rundown takes up to 30 seconds). 2. Switch the main isolator Q1 to OFF and lock it with your personal padlock. Attach a danger tag with your name. 3. Press the hydraulic pressure release valve V3 until the gauge reads 0 bar. 4. Check for zero energy: press START; the press must not start. 5. Punch tips and die edges are sharp: wear cut-resistant gloves when handling tooling. 6. Wear the dust mask and gloves listed in the batch manufacturing record for the product on the press.

Run the turret empty at 10 rpm for 2 minutes and listen for abnormal noise. 4. Run the first tablets and give them to QA for in-process checks (weight, thickness, hardness) before the batch continues. 5. Do line clearance as per the plant SOP. 6. Record the repair, the parts used and the downtime in the equipment logbook.

guide.title: AC-2 Door seal fault: inspect and replace door gasket
guide.summary: A possible cause is a cut, flattened, or hardened door gasket, or low air pressure, triggering a door seal fault at cycle start. This guide is based on manual section 4.2 and past incident PHA-0028, where the door gasket had a cut near the hinge. Work involves safety lockout, cleaning the groove, fitting gasket SA-DG-600 with grease SA-SG-01, and test cycles.

safety.text: Never try to open the door unless the chamber pressure gauge reads 0 bar and chamber temperature is below 80 °C.
Abort the cycle, close steam supply valve SV-1, and lock it.
Switch electrical isolator Q0 to OFF, lock it, and attach danger tags.
Open chamber vent valve and verify both chamber and jacket pressure gauges read 0 bar.
Wear heat-resistant gloves and a face shield because pipes, door, and chamber surfaces stay hot.

steps.text: Lock out the sterilizer and ensure the chamber is at 0 bar and below 80 °C.
Inspect the whole gasket for cuts, flat spots, and hardening, checking carefully near the bottom hinge.
Remove the damaged door gasket from the groove.
Clean the gasket groove thoroughly using a lint-free cloth and water for injection.
Press new door gasket SA-DG-600 evenly into the groove starting at the top centre.
Apply a thin film of approved silicone grease SA-SG-01 to the new door gasket.
Check that the plant compressed air supply is at least 5 bar.

restart_checks.text: Remove locks and tags, open SV-1 slowly, and allow the jacket to heat up.
Run a vacuum leak test and verify the leak rate is 1.3 mbar/min or less.
Run a Bowie-Dick test cycle and verify the indicator sheet shows an even colour change.
Have QA review the test results and release the sterilizer.
Record the repair, test results, and downtime in the equipment logbook.

The vacuum leak test exceeds the 1.3 mbar/min limit after replacing the gasket.
The Bowie-Dick test indicator sheet does not show an even colour change.

manual_sections.manual_title: Sterimax SA-600 Steam Sterilizer: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 4.2 E-07 Door seal fault
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-07, door seal pressure not reached within 60 seconds of cycle start; the cycle does not start or is aborted. Likely causes: a cut, flattened or hardened door gasket; dirt in the gasket groove; low compressed air supply (below 5 bar); a faulty seal supply valve. Procedure: 1. Lock out the sterilizer and make sure the chamber is at 0 bar and below 80 °C (section 1.4). 2. Inspect the whole gasket for cuts, flat spots and hardening, especially near the hinge. 3. Clean the groove with a lint-free cloth and water for injection. 4. Replace a damaged gasket with door gasket SA-DG-600: press it evenly into the groove starting at the top centre, and apply a thin film of approved silicone grease SA-SG-01. 5. Check compressed air supply is at least 5 bar. 6. Run a vacuum leak test (limit 1.3 mbar/min) and a Bowie-Dick test; both must pass before the sterilizer is released. Typical time: 90 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Sterimax SA-600 Steam Sterilizer: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 1.4 Pressure, steam and lockout
manual_sections.text: The chamber and jacket hold steam under pressure. 1. Never try to open the door unless the chamber pressure gauge reads 0 bar and the chamber temperature is below 80 °C. 2. Before any repair, end or abort the cycle, close the steam supply valve SV-1 and lock it; switch the electrical isolator Q0 to OFF and lock it; attach danger tags. 3. Open the chamber vent valve and wait until the chamber and jacket gauges both read 0 bar. 4. Pipes, door and chamber surfaces stay hot: wear heat-resistant gloves and a face shield.

manual_sections.title: 4.3 E-12 Vacuum level not reached
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-12, the chamber does not reach the pre-vacuum set point; the cycle aborts. Likely causes: no seal water to the liquid ring vacuum pump, an air leak at the door gasket or a valve, a worn vacuum pump. Procedure: 1. Check the seal water flow to the vacuum pump (sight glass must show flow). 2. Run a vacuum leak test: above 1.3 mbar/min means a leak; check the door gasket first (section 4.2). 3. If there is no leak, ask maintenance to service the pump with kit SA-VP-KIT. Typical time: 60 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Sterimax SA-600 Steam Sterilizer: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 2.1 Machine overview
manual_sections.text: The SA-600 is a jacketed steam sterilizer with a hinged door. The door seals with an inflatable silicone gasket that sits in a groove around the door frame and is pressed against the door by compressed air during the cycle. A liquid ring vacuum pump removes air during the pre-vacuum pulses. Condensate leaves the chamber through the drain, where a PT100 sensor measures drain temperature, then through strainer ST-2 and the steam trap.

Run a Bowie-Dick test cycle: the indicator sheet must show an even colour change. 4. QA reviews the test results and releases the sterilizer. 5. guide.title: BL-3 Forming Temperature Alarm: Test and Replace Forming Heater Cartridge
guide.summary: A possible cause is a failed forming plate heater cartridge or an unseated thermocouple. This guide is based on equipment manual section 5.2 and repeat incident PHA-0026. The procedure covers electrical testing, cartridge replacement, and restart checks.

safety.text: Stop the machine using the STOP key at the end of a cycle.
Turn main switch S0 to OFF, lock it with your personal padlock, and attach a danger tag.
Close the compressed air ball valve and open dump valve DV1 until the air gauge reads 0 bar.
Press START to confirm zero energy; the machine must not move.
Wait until plate temperature displays below 50 °C before touching, or wear heat-resistant gloves.

steps.text: Apply lockout/tagout and confirm the machine is safe and de-energized.
steps.caution: Plates can reach up to 160 °C; verify temperature is below 50 °C or wear heat-resistant gloves.

steps.text: Disconnect the forming heater cartridges at the terminal box.
Measure the electrical resistance of each heater cartridge using a multimeter.
steps.caution: A good cartridge reads 40 to 50 ohm; an open circuit means the cartridge has failed.

steps.text: Remove any failed heater cartridge and install a new cartridge BPM-HC-250.
Inspect the thermocouple to ensure it sits fully inside its bore and the clamp is tight.
Refit the thermocouple using heat-transfer paste BPM-HP-02, or replace it with BPM-TC-K2 if damaged.
Close guards, remove your lock and tag, and allow the machine to heat up for 20 minutes.
Run empty strips and check pocket depth on 10 strips.

manual_sections.title: 5.2 E-31 Forming heater temperature low
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-31, forming plate temperature more than 10 °C below the set point; pockets come out shallow or uneven and the machine stops. Likely causes: a failed heater cartridge, a loose or failed thermocouple, a failed solid-state relay. Procedure: 1. Lock out the machine and let the plates cool (section 1.3). 2. Disconnect the heater cartridges at the terminal box and measure each one: a good cartridge reads 40 to 50 ohm; open circuit means failed. Replace a failed cartridge with BPM-HC-250 (250 W, 230 V). 3. Check that the thermocouple sits fully in its bore and the clamp is tight. Refit it with heat-transfer paste BPM-HP-02; replace a damaged thermocouple with BPM-TC-K2. 4. If cartridges and thermocouple are good, ask the electrician to check solid-state relay BPM-SSR-40. 5. Heat up for 20 minutes and check pocket depth on 10 strips. Typical time: 60 minutes.

manual_sections.title: 5.3 E-44 Sealing temperature deviation
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-44, sealing plate temperature outside set point plus or minus 5 °C; risk of leaking blisters. The machine stops. Likely causes: failed sealing heater cartridge, thermocouple not in contact, display showing the controller set point instead of the actual temperature. Procedure: 1. Lock out and cool down (section 1.3). 2. Measure the sealing heater cartridges (40 to 50 ohm). Replace failed ones with BPM-HC-250. 3. Reseat the thermocouple with heat-transfer paste BPM-HP-02. 4. After heat-up, check the plate surface temperature with a calibrated contact thermometer; it must be within 5 °C of the set point. 5. Run a blue dye leak test on 20 blisters from each lane before restarting the batch. Typical time: 60 minutes.

manual_sections.title: 5.4 E-52 Film web break
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-52, the PVC web is broken or the film reel has run out; the machine stops. Likely causes: a bad splice, too high web tension, a worn or seized guide roller, film stuck to a hot forming plate. Procedure: 1. Lock out the machine (section 1.3). 2. Remove the broken film from the forming station. 3. Rethread the film along the path shown in the figure, under the dancer arm. 4. Check every guide roller turns freely; replace a seized roller with BPM-GR-08. 5. Join the film with splice tape, keeping the splice straight. 6. Run 5 empty cycles at low speed and check the web runs centred. Typical time: 20 minutes.

manual_sections.title: 5.5 W-12 Film tracking deviation
manual_sections.text: Warning W-12 appears when the film edge sensor sees the web more than 2 mm off centre. The machine keeps running. First actions: check the film reel is pushed fully onto the unwind shaft and the reel core is not damaged; clean the edge sensor; adjust the web guide by turning the tracking knob a quarter turn at a time. Repeated W-12 warnings often come before an E-52 web break.

manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-60, cut blister cards stuck in the punching die; the machine stops. Likely causes: a blunt punching die, misaligned perforation, foil build-up. Procedure: 1. Lock out (section 1.3). 2. Remove the stuck cards and foil pieces with plastic tweezers. 3. Inspect the punch and die edges; a blunt or chipped die set must be replaced with BPM-PD-01 by maintenance. 4. Check card position against the punch with one slow cycle. Typical time: 35 minutes.

guide.title: BL-3 E-52: clear web break and rethread film
guide.summary: The machine stopped due to alarm E-52 with a broken film web. Possible causes include a bad splice, excessive web tension, film sticking to hot plates, or a seized guide roller. This guide is based on manufacturer procedures for web break recovery and safety lockout.

safety.text: Stop the machine using the STOP key at the end of a cycle.
Switch the main switch S0 to OFF, lock it with your padlock, and attach a danger tag.
Close the compressed air ball valve and open dump valve DV1 until the gauge reads 0 bar.
Wait until plate temperature on the display is below 50 °C before touching plates, or wear heat-resistant gloves.
Press START to verify zero energy; the machine must not move.

steps.text: Lock out the machine and release air pressure.
steps.caution: Plates can reach 160 °C; ensure they are below 50 °C or wear heat-resistant gloves.

steps.text: Remove the broken film from the forming station.
Rethread the film along the path and under the dancer arm.
Check that every guide roller turns freely by hand.
Replace any seized roller with a new guide roller BPM-GR-08.
Join the film with splice tape, keeping the splice straight.
Run 5 empty cycles at low speed and verify the web runs centred.

restart_checks.text: Remove tools, close guards, and remove your lock and tag.
Heat up the machine for 20 minutes.
Run empty strips and check pocket shape, seal pattern, and batch code.
Perform a blue dye leak test on 20 blisters from each lane; all must pass before feeding tablets.
Obtain QA check on the first cards before continuing the batch.
Complete line clearance per plant SOP and record repair in equipment logbook.

escalate_if: A guide roller is seized and replacement BPM-GR-08 cannot be fitted.
Alarm E-52 immediately recurs after rethreading and splicing the film.
The web tracks more than 2 mm off-centre or triggers repeated W-12 warnings.
Forming plates show physical damage or severe film adhesion.

Inspect the punch and die edges; a blunt or chipped die set must be replaced with BPM-PD-01 by maintenance. 4. Check card position against the punch with one slow cycle. Typical time: 35 minutes.

manual_sections.title: 5.2 E-31 Forming heater temperature low
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-31, forming plate temperature more than 10 °C below the set point; pockets come out shallow or uneven and the machine stops. Likely causes: a failed heater cartridge, a loose or failed thermocouple, a failed solid-state relay. Procedure: 1. Lock out the machine and let the plates cool (section 1.3). 2. Disconnect the heater cartridges at the terminal box and measure each one: a good cartridge reads 40 to 50 ohm; open circuit means failed. Replace a failed cartridge with BPM-HC-250 (250 W, 230 V). 3. Check that the thermocouple sits fully in its bore and the clamp is tight. Refit it with heat-transfer paste BPM-HP-02; replace a damaged thermocouple with BPM-TC-K2. 4. If cartridges and thermocouple are good, ask the electrician to check solid-state relay BPM-SSR-40. 5. Heat up for 20 minutes and check pocket depth on 10 strips. Typical time: 60 minutes.

manual_sections.title: 5.3 E-44 Sealing temperature deviation
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-44, sealing plate temperature outside set point plus or minus 5 °C; risk of leaking blisters. The machine stops. Likely causes: failed sealing heater cartridge, thermocouple not in contact, display showing the controller set point instead of the actual temperature. Procedure: 1. Lock out and cool down (section 1.3). 2. Measure the sealing heater cartridges (40 to 50 ohm). Replace failed ones with BPM-HC-250. 3. Reseat the thermocouple with heat-transfer paste BPM-HP-02. 4. After heat-up, check the plate surface temperature with a calibrated contact thermometer; it must be within 5 °C of the set point. 5. Run a blue dye leak test on 20 blisters from each lane before restarting the batch. Typical time: 60 minutes.

manual_sections.title: 6.6 W-305 Lubrication pressure low
manual_sections.text: Warning W-305 appears when the central lubrication pressure is below 2 bar. The press keeps running, but punch guides and cam tracks are no longer oiled. manual_sections.title: 6.2 E-104 Upper punch tight
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-104 PUNCH TIGHT, the turret stops and the main drive torque is high. Likely causes: product fines packed in an upper punch guide bore; too little punch lubrication; a scored, burred or mushroomed punch; a worn guide bushing; wear on the upper cam track. Procedure: 1. Lock out the press (section 1.2). 2. Open the upper guard. Turn the turret slowly with handwheel H1 and feel for the station that resists; mark it. 3. Remove the upper punch from that station with punch removal tool T-12. 4. Inspect the punch barrel, head and tip for scoring, burrs or a mushroomed head. A damaged punch must be replaced with upper punch RTP-PN-U-10; never polish the barrel. 5. Clean the guide bore with a lint-free cloth moistened with 70% IPA. Never use a metal brush. 6. Check the bore with go/no-go gauge G-19. If the gauge does not pass, the guide bushing is worn: replace bushing RTP-BS-07 (maintenance engineer only, section 9.4). 7. Put 1 drop of food-grade punch oil RTP-LB-02 on the punch barrel and wipe off the excess. 8. Refit the punch and its dust cup RTP-SL-03. Turn the turret two full turns with H1: it must turn without resistance. Typical time: 45 minutes for one station; about 3 hours if a guide bushing must be replaced.

manual_sections.title: 6.3 E-118 Lower punch tight or ejection fault
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-118, the turret stops at ejection or a lower punch sticks below the die table. Likely causes: powder under the die table, a lower punch with a damaged tip or barrel, a worn ejection cam, a die not seated flush. Procedure: 1. Lock out the press (section 1.2). 2. Remove the die table scraper and vacuum the powder from the lower turret. 3. Turn the turret with handwheel H1 and find the tight lower punch. 4. Remove it through the lower punch access door with tool T-14 and inspect it. Replace a damaged punch with lower punch RTP-PN-L-10. 5. Check that the die is flush with the die table using the dial gauge: maximum 0.05 mm proud. Reseat or replace die RTP-DI-10. 6. Inspect the ejection cam for grooves; report wear to the engineer. guide.title: AC-2 E-12: Troubleshoot vacuum fault and check door seal or pump
guide.summary: Alarm E-12 indicates the chamber failed to reach the pre-vacuum set point, with possible causes being lack of seal water, a door gasket or valve leak, or pump wear. This guide follows the standard manual troubleshooting procedure to verify water flow, run leak tests, and service seals or the pump. QA and maintenance must confirm test results before returning the sterilizer to service.

safety.text: Never open the door unless the chamber pressure gauge reads 0 bar and chamber temperature is below 80 °C.
Close and lock steam supply valve SV-1, switch electrical isolator Q0 to OFF and lock it, and attach danger tags.
Open the chamber vent valve and wait until chamber and jacket gauges both read 0 bar.
Wear heat-resistant gloves and a face shield because pipes, door, and chamber surfaces stay hot.

steps.text: Check the seal water flow to the liquid ring vacuum pump through the sight glass.
steps.caution: The sight glass must show flow before proceeding.

steps.text: Run a vacuum leak test on the sterilizer.
steps.caution: A leak rate above 1.3 mbar/min means an air leak is present.

steps.text: Inspect the inflatable silicone door gasket in the door frame groove for damage or leaks if the leak test fails.
Replace the damaged door gasket with spare part SA-DG-600 if a leak is found.
Lock out the sterilizer at valve SV-1 and isolator Q0 if pump servicing is required.
steps.caution: Verify chamber and jacket pressure gauges read 0 bar before touching internal components.

steps.text: Service the liquid ring vacuum pump using vacuum pump service kit SA-VP-KIT if no air leak was found.

restart_checks.text: Remove locks and tags, open SV-1 slowly, and let the jacket heat up.
Run a vacuum leak test and confirm the leak rate is 1.3 mbar/min or less.
Run a Bowie-Dick test cycle and verify the indicator sheet shows an even colour change.
Ensure QA reviews the test results and formally releases the sterilizer.
Record the repair, test results, and downtime in the equipment logbook.

escalate_if: No seal water flow can be established to the vacuum pump.
Vacuum leak rate remains above 1.3 mbar/min after checking the door gasket.

manual_sections.title: 2.1 Machine overview
manual_sections.text: The SA-600 is a jacketed steam sterilizer with a hinged door. The door seals with an inflatable silicone gasket that sits in a groove around the door frame and is pressed against the door by compressed air during the cycle. A liquid ring vacuum pump removes air during the pre-vacuum pulses. Condensate leaves the chamber through the drain, where a PT100 sensor measures drain temperature, then through strainer ST-2 and the steam trap.

manual_sections.title: 4.4 E-21 Drain temperature low
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-21, drain temperature below 121 °C during the exposure phase; the cycle aborts and the load is not sterile. Likely causes: strainer ST-2 blocked with scale, a stuck steam trap, wet steam. Procedure: 1. Lock out the sterilizer (section 1.4). 2. Open the strainer cap and clean screen ST-2; replace a damaged screen with SA-STR-2. 3. Blow down the steam trap; replace a trap that stays closed with SA-ST-15. 4. Check the PT100 drain sensor reading against a calibrated probe; replace a faulty sensor with SA-PT100. 5. Run one empty cycle and check drain temperature stays at or above 121 °C for the whole exposure. The aborted load must be treated as not sterile and reported to QA. Typical time: 60 minutes.

Run a Bowie-Dick test cycle: the indicator sheet must show an even colour change. 4. QA reviews the test results and releases the sterilizer. 5. manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 9.6 Return to service after a repair
manual_sections.text: 1. Remove all tools and check that every punch and die is in place. 2. Close all guards and remove your lock and tag. 3. Run the turret empty at 10 rpm for 2 minutes and listen for abnormal noise. 4. Run the first tablets and give them to QA for in-process checks (weight, thickness, hardness) before the batch continues. 5. Do line clearance as per the plant SOP. 6. Record the repair, the parts used and the downtime in the equipment logbook.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.2 E-104 Upper punch tight
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-104 PUNCH TIGHT, the turret stops and the main drive torque is high. Likely causes: product fines packed in an upper punch guide bore; too little punch lubrication; a scored, burred or mushroomed punch; a worn guide bushing; wear on the upper cam track. Procedure: 1. Lock out the press (section 1.2). 2. Open the upper guard. Turn the turret slowly with handwheel H1 and feel for the station that resists; mark it. 3. Remove the upper punch from that station with punch removal tool T-12. 4. Inspect the punch barrel, head and tip for scoring, burrs or a mushroomed head. A damaged punch must be replaced with upper punch RTP-PN-U-10; never polish the barrel. 5. Clean the guide bore with a lint-free cloth moistened with 70% IPA. Never use a metal brush. 6. Check the bore with go/no-go gauge G-19. If the gauge does not pass, the guide bushing is worn: replace bushing RTP-BS-07 (maintenance engineer only, section 9.4). 7. Put 1 drop of food-grade punch oil RTP-LB-02 on the punch barrel and wipe off the excess. 8. Refit the punch and its dust cup RTP-SL-03. Turn the turret two full turns with H1: it must turn without resistance. Typical time: 45 minutes for one station; about 3 hours if a guide bushing must be replaced.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.5 W-212 Compression force deviation
manual_sections.text: Warning W-212 appears when the main compression force is more than 10% away from the set point over 50 tablets. The press keeps running. Likely causes: uneven die fill (hopper level, feed frame paddle speed, poor powder flow), lower punches of unequal working length, fines building up in punch guides. First actions: check the hopper level and feed frame speed; weigh 20 tablets and compare with the batch record limits. If W-212 appears more than 10 times in an hour, check punch working length with gauge G-21 at the next stop. Rising W-212 counts together with a higher main drive torque often come before an E-104 punch tight stop.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.1 Alarm list
manual_sections.text: Alarms starting with E stop the press. Alarms starting with W are warnings: the press keeps running but the cause must be checked. E-104 Upper punch tight. E-118 Lower punch tight or ejection fault. E-150 Guard open. E-221 Main drive overload. E-330 Feed frame motor fault. W-212 Compression force deviation. W-305 Lubrication pressure low. W-401 Hopper level low.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.3 E-118 Lower punch tight or ejection fault
manual_sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-118, the turret stops at ejection or a lower punch sticks below the die table. Likely causes: powder under the die table, a lower punch with a damaged tip or barrel, a worn ejection cam, a die not seated flush. Procedure: 1. Lock out the press (section 1.2). 2. Remove the die table scraper and vacuum the powder from the lower turret. 3. Turn the turret with handwheel H1 and find the tight lower punch. 4. Remove it through the lower punch access door with tool T-14 and inspect it. Replace a damaged punch with lower punch RTP-PN-L-10. 5. Check that the die is flush with the die table using the dial gauge: maximum 0.05 mm proud. Reseat or replace die RTP-DI-10. 6. Inspect the ejection cam for grooves; report wear to the engineer. Typical time: 50 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 6.6 W-305 Lubrication pressure low
manual_sections.text: Warning W-305 appears when the central lubrication pressure is below 2 bar. The press keeps running, but punch guides and cam tracks are no longer oiled. Running for long with W-305 leads to punch tightness (E-104). First actions: check the oil level in the central lubrication reservoir and top up with oil RTP-LB-01 only. Check the lines and the distributor block for leaks or a blocked line. Run the lubrication pump manually from the maintenance screen until pressure is above 2 bar. Typical time: 20 minutes.

manual_sections.manual_title: Kestrel RTP-37 Rotary Tablet Press: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)
manual_sections.title: 1.2 Lockout before opening any guard
manual_sections.text: Never open a guard or put hands near the turret while the press can move. 1. Stop the press with the STOP key and wait until the turret has stopped completely (rundown takes up to 30 seconds). 2. Switch the main isolator Q1 to OFF and lock it with your personal padlock. Attach a danger tag with your name. 3. Press the hydraulic pressure release valve V3 until the gauge reads 0 bar. 4. Check for zero energy: press START; the press must not start. 5. Punch tips and die edges are sharp: wear cut-resistant gloves when handling tooling. 6. Wear the dust mask and gloves listed in the batch manufacturing record for the product on the press.
